protocol.description:
Tontoo UI protocol for declarative, server-side rendered surfaces.
This protocol allows client applications to describe their user interface as a declarative widget tree which is transmitted to the TontooOS compositor for server-side rendering. The compositor owns the rendering pipeline — clients never upload buffers or draw pixels.
Clients bind the tontoo_ui_manager global, create a tontoo_ui_surface for each top-level window, and push widget-tree snapshots via update_widget_tree. The compositor sends back configure events for sizing and interactive events (clicks, hovers, key input) that clients handle in their application logic.
The same object also carries the backdrop stream: a client rendered window asks for the pixels behind itself (set_backdrop, create_backdrop_buffer) and receives them in a shared file (backdrop), which lets it run its own frosted-glass blur instead of paying for a compositor side Gaussian blur on every frame.

interface.name: tontoo_ui_manager
interface.summary: Singleton manager for Tontoo UI surfaces

description.summary: Create Tontoo UI surfaces

interface.description: The tontoo_ui_manager global is the entry point for the Tontoo UI protocol. Clients bind this global and use it to create individual tontoo_ui_surface objects, one per top-level window.

event.name: ping

description.summary: Ping the client to elicit a pong

event.description: A ping event is sent by the compositor to check whether the client is still responsive. The client should respond with a pong request containing the same serial.

request.name: get_tontoo_ui_surface

description.summary: Create a new Tontoo UI surface

request.description: Create a new tontoo_ui_surface associated with the given id. Each surface corresponds to a single top-level application window.

request.name: pong

description.summary: Respond to a ping event

request.description: A pong request is sent in response to a ping event from the compositor. The serial must match the most recent ping event received.

interface.name: tontoo_ui_surface
interface.summary: A single application surface rendered via widget tree

description.summary: Declarative UI surface

interface.description:
A tontoo_ui_surface represents one application window. The client describes its UI declaratively by pushing serialized widget trees and the compositor renders them server-side.
The widget tree is encoded as a flat array of serialized nodes. Each entry in the array is a widget node described by a type tag followed by its typed fields. Nodes are referenced by their array index (node_id). Container nodes list their children by index.
The serialization format is documented separately; the compositor and the TontooUI client library agree on the canonical encoding.

request.name: set_title

description.summary: Set the window title

request.description: Set a descriptive title for this surface. The compositor may use this for window lists, task bars, and accessibility labels.

request.name: set_size

description.summary: Set the preferred window size

request.description: Request the compositor to resize this surface to the given dimensions in logical pixels. The compositor may adjust the final size based on screen constraints and send a configure event with the actual dimensions.

request.name: set_glass

description.summary: Configure glass (blur) effect parameters

request.description:
Set the frosted-glass visual effect for this surface. The compositor applies a Gaussian blur to content behind the surface with the given parameters.
The compositor does not blur client rendered windows; it only draws the tint quad for widget tree surfaces. Client rendered apps ask for the raw backdrop instead and run their own blur, see set_backdrop.

arg.name: milkiness
arg.summary: Blur milkiness (0.0 = clear, 1.0 = fully opaque frosted glass)

arg.name: alpha
arg.summary: Background tint alpha (0.0 = no tint, 1.0 = fully tinted)

arg.name: sigma
arg.summary: Blur radius sigma in logical pixels

request.name: create_backdrop_buffer

description.summary: Hand over the shared buffer for backdrop frames

request.description:
The client allocates a shared memory file (memfd_create or a file in /dev/shm), sizes it to stride * height and maps it read-write. It passes the file descriptor here and keeps its own mapping.
The compositor maps the same file read-write and writes the pixels of every backdrop frame into it. The layout is Xrgb8888, top-down, stride bytes per row, width times height pixels. A new frame is announced with the backdrop event; the client answers with ack_backdrop once it copied the pixels out.
The buffer holds the whole output so that a moving window does not require a new allocation; only the window rect inside it is overwritten.

request.name: set_backdrop

description.summary: Subscribe to the desktop backdrop of a window

request.description:
Ask the compositor to stream the pixels behind wl_surface_id so the client can render its own backdrop blur. Enable while backdrop glass is on screen and disable again afterwards; the compositor only captures while the flag is set and only recaptures when the client acknowledged the previous frame or when the window moved, was resized or the frame damage touched its rect.
wl_surface_id is the protocol id of the client's own wl_surface. Object ids are per client, so the value is only meaningful when both objects live on the same connection.

arg.name: scale
arg.summary: Downscale divisor (1, 2 or 4); 0 means the default of 2

arg.name: wl_surface_id
arg.summary: Protocol id of the wl_surface to capture behind

request.name: ack_backdrop

description.summary: Confirm that a backdrop frame was copied

request.description: Tells the compositor the client is done reading the frame with this serial, so the next capture may overwrite the buffer. The compositor skips capturing entirely while a frame is unacked, which keeps glReadPixels stalls off the idle path.

request.name: update_widget_tree

description.summary: Push a new declarative widget tree snapshot

request.description:
Replace the entire widget tree for this surface with a new serialized snapshot. The argument is an array of bytes containing the serialized widget tree.
The serialization is a compact binary encoding where each node consists of: - A uint32 type tag identifying the widget variant - Type-specific fields encoded in wire format - For containers: a uint32 child count followed by child node_id references
Node IDs are implicit — they correspond to the index of the node in the serialized array, starting from 0.
Sending a new widget tree is atomic: the compositor replaces the previous tree entirely on receipt. Partial updates are not supported.

request.name: set_color_scheme

description.summary: Set the preferred color scheme

request.description: Tell the compositor which color scheme this surface prefers. The compositor may use this to adjust glass tint, shadows, and other visual properties.

request.name: request_close

description.summary: Request the compositor to close this surface

request.description: The client asks the compositor to close this window. The compositor may honour the request directly or present a confirmation dialog first.

request.name: request_minimize

description.summary: Request the compositor to minimize this surface

request.description: Ask the compositor to minimize (hide) this window.

request.name: request_maximize

description.summary: Request the compositor to maximize this surface

request.description: Ask the compositor to maximize this window to fill the available output area.

event.name: configure

description.summary: Configure the surface geometry

event.description: The compositor sends a configure event to inform the client of the final surface dimensions. The client should update its widget tree to match the provided size.

event.name: backdrop

description.summary: A new desktop backdrop frame is available

event.description:
Sent after the compositor wrote the pixels behind the watched wl_surface into the buffer passed with create_backdrop_buffer.
x, y, width and height are physical output pixels and describe the window rect inside the buffer. scale is the downscale divisor: consecutive pixels of the frame are scale buffer pixels apart, so a client samples every scale-th pixel of every scale-th row.
The client must copy the frame out before sending ack_backdrop.

arg.name: x
arg.summary: Region origin x in buffer pixels

arg.name: y
arg.summary: Region origin y in buffer pixels

event.name: close

description.summary: The compositor requests the surface to close

event.description: Sent when the compositor decides the surface should close (e.g. user clicked the close button). The client should tear down its surface and exit.

event.name: widget_clicked

description.summary: A widget node was clicked by the user

event.description: Emitted when the user clicks on a widget node within this surface. The node_id corresponds to the index of the widget node in the most recently received widget tree. The client should inspect the widget type and handle the interaction accordingly.

arg.name: node_id
arg.summary: Index of the clicked node in the widget tree

event.name: widget_hovered

description.summary: The pointer entered or moved over a widget node

event.description: Emitted when the pointer enters or moves to a different widget node. The client can use this to update hover visual states. node_id 0 with no further events indicates the pointer left all interactive widgets.

arg.name: node_id
arg.summary: Index of the hovered node in the widget tree, 0 if none

event.name: key_event

description.summary: A keyboard event directed at this surface

event.description: Forwarded keyboard events from the compositor. The key field is an evdev key code. The state field is 1 for key-down and 0 for key-up.
